blocks.source: Vol IV, Policy Training, § Real-Robot Fine-Tuning and Residual Control
blocks.md: Fine-tuning a simulation-trained policy directly on a physical robot to absorb a small fixture offset can fix the local contact error while overheating the motor windings, spending gearbox fatigue life on exploratory impacts, and silently corrupting the free-space approach trajectories that had already passed qualification. Mechanical assemblies rarely match their models exactly: on a warehouse cage door, for example, the physical strike plate may sit at a small mounting offset relative to its nominal position in the simulation model.

questions.q: The section **Real-Robot Fine-Tuning and Residual Control** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: The policy manifest records how a checkpoint was produced (regime sequence, base digest, inference contract, data support, omission log, wear log) and computes the declared ODD as support minus omissions.

A decoder chosen for multimodality must fit the proposal deadline, since latency is encoding plus every dependent decoder evaluation, so the head and evaluation count that training picks decide schedulability.
A trial campaign's wall clock is trials times rollout plus reset over rigs (about 93 days of execution for 10^6 latch trials before resets), and every trial spends heat and drivetrain life.
Sim-to-real mismatch decomposes into dynamics, sensing, appearance, and timing channels, each sized by paired probing, and randomization covers modeled parameters but never omitted mechanisms.
